desc:
prices[i] is the price of a stock on day i. On every day you may perform at most one action: buy one share, sell one share, or do nothing. You may own at most m shares at any moment and you start with none. Shares you still own after the last day are worth nothing, so you will want to sell them before that.

Return the maximum total profit.

Example: prices = [1,2,4,3,5,6]. With m = 1 the answer is 6 (1 to 4, then 3 to 6). With m = 2 it is 9: buy on days 0, 1 and 3, sell on days 2, 4 and 5, earning 3 + 3 + 3.
hints: With m = 1 this is the unlimited-transactions problem. What extra thing must a day remember when several shares may be owned?
Remember how many shares you own right now: j between 0 and m. Let dp[j] be the best cash balance while owning j shares.
For each price p build a new array: keep dp[j], or buy (dp[j-1] - p), or sell (dp[j+1] + p) and take the maximum. Start with dp[0] = 0 and the others at -infinity; the answer is dp[0] at the end.
editorial: The only thing that matters for the future is the day and the number of shares in your hands, so use a DP over (day, shares owned). dp[j] is the best cash after the current day with j shares owned; cash already accounts for the purchase prices of those shares.

On a new price p, the options for the new count j are: do nothing (dp[j]), buy one (dp[j-1] - p, needs j ≥ 1) or sell one (dp[j+1] + p, needs j < m). Because only one action is allowed per day, the new array must be built from the old one, not updated in place.
Leftover shares are worth nothing, so the best final answer owns zero shares: dp[0]. The work is O(n · m) time and O(m) space.
